mainTopic: Mourning before תשעה באב, the limits on the סעודה המפסקת, and the rules of the fast day itself
overview: The amud opens by finishing the explanation of how רבי מאיר, רבי יהודה and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל each learn their view on pre-תשעה באב mourning from a different word in one פסוק. רבא then rules leniently: like רבן שמעון בן גמליאל on when the mourning starts, and like רבי מאיר on when it ends. Next the גמרא turns to the משנה's ban on two cooked dishes on ערב תשעה באב, and רב יהודה limits it to the afternoon and to the final meal before the fast (סעודה המפסקת). Several ברייתות back up these limits and add views on meat, wine and bathing at that meal. Then a ברייתא teaches that all the practices of an אבל apply on תשעה באב itself, including a ban on learning joyful תורה, with exceptions for sad books like איוב and קינות. The גמרא returns to the meal and allows salted meat and fresh wine, defining how long each must be kept. The amud ends with the start of a story about the simple bread-and-salt meal of רבי יהודה ברבי אילעאי, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Each opinion's source in the same verse
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes showing how each of the three opinions about pre-תשעה באב mourning comes from a different word in the פסוק 'חגה חדשה ושבתה'.
steps.simpleTranslation: The one who says the mourning starts from ראש חודש learns it from 'her festival.' The one who says the whole month is forbidden learns it from 'her month.' The one who says only that whole week is forbidden learns it from 'her Shabbat.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing its explanation of how all three תנאים read the same פסוק (הושע 2:13) and each finds his own opinion in a different word.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר (from ראש חודש until the fast) learns from 'חגה', since ראש חודש is treated like a festival. רבי יהודה (the whole month) learns from 'חדשה'. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל (only the week of תשעה באב) learns from 'שבתה', because here שבת means a week.

keyTerms.meaning: The one who says (the opinion that holds...)
Her festival; here it points to ראש חודש
Her month; points to the entire month
Her Shabbat; here it means her week

steps.confusionAlert: Don't read 'שבת' here as the seventh day. In this derivation it means the week in which תשעה באב falls.

phrases.english: from "her festival."
phrases.notes: This finishes the sentence from before: the one who says the mourning starts from ראש חודש learns it from this word in הושע 2:13.

phrases.english: And the one who says the whole (month) is forbidden —
from "her month,"

phrases.aramaic: וּמַאן דְּאָמַר כׇּל הַשַּׁבָּת כּוּלָּהּ אָסוּר —
phrases.english: and the one who says the entire week is forbidden —
from "her Shabbat."
phrases.notes: Here 'Shabbat' means a week, the week of תשעה באב.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַאן דְּאָמַר כּוּלּוֹ אָסוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רבי יוחנן's statement, begun just before this section, that all three opinions come from one verse.
steps.raayaObject: The three opinions of רבי מאיר, רבי יהודה and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל on how long the mourning practices last before תשעה באב.
steps.raayaSupportSource: הושע 2:13: 'והשבתי כל משושה חגה חדשה ושבתה', with each word supporting a different opinion.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the three opinions are not random. Each one reads the same פסוק and stresses a different word.

steps.title: רבא rules like both רבן שמעון בן גמליאל and רבי מאיר
steps.stepSummary: רבא gives two rulings: the הלכה follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, and it also follows רבי מאיר. Both rulings go the lenient way.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: The הלכה follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל. And רבא also said: The הלכה follows רבי מאיר. Both rulings are meant to be lenient.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא decides the practical הלכה by taking the lenient side of two different opinions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל is more lenient about when the mourning starts: only the week of תשעה באב, not from ראש חודש. רבי מאיר is more lenient about when it ends: it lasts only until the fast, not afterward. רבא takes each opinion only where it is lenient.
steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not contradicting himself. He follows each תנא only on the point where that תנא is more lenient.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רָבָא: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל.
phrases.english: Rava said: The halakha is in accordance with Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel.
And Rava said: The halakha is in accordance with Rabbi Meir.
And both of them are for leniency,

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the sources of the opinions to deciding the practical הלכה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The mourning practices apply only during the week of תשעה באב (like רבן שמעון בן גמליאל) and end at the fast (like רבי מאיר).
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the practical ruling about when the pre-תשעה באב restrictions begin and end.

steps.title: Why the ruling like רבן שמעון בן גמליאל is needed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that the ruling like רבי מאיר alone would have suggested the mourning starts at ראש חודש. So רבא also had to rule like רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Both rulings are needed. If רבא had only told us the הלכה follows רבי מאיר, I would have thought the mourning starts at ראש חודש. So he tells us the הלכה follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers an unspoken question: why did רבא need two rulings? This step explains the first half.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With only the ruling like רבי מאיר, we would have taken all of his opinion, including the early start at ראש חודש. The ruling like רבן שמעון בן גמליאל moves the start to the week of תשעה באב.

keyTerms.meaning: It is necessary (both statements are needed)

phrases.english: And it is necessary. For if he had taught us
the halakha is like Rabbi Meir,
I would have said: even from the New Moon,

phrases.aramaic: קָמַשְׁמַע לַן הֲלָכָה כְּרַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל.
phrases.english: so it teaches us the halakha is like Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּצְרִיכָא. דְּאִי אַשְׁמוֹעִינַן הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why רבא's second ruling (like רבן שמעון בן גמליאל) is not extra.
steps.terutzResolutionType: צריכותא: showing that each statement teaches something the other does not
steps.terutzHavaAmina: With only the ruling like רבי מאיר, the restrictions would start at ראש חודש.
steps.terutzMaskana: Ruling like רבן שמעון בן גמליאל limits the start to the week of תשעה באב.

steps.title: Why the ruling like רבי מאיר is needed
steps.stepSummary: With only the ruling like רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, we might think the restrictions go on after the fast for the rest of the week. So רבא also rules like רבי מאיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if רבא had only told us the הלכה follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, I would have thought the restrictions apply even after תשעה באב. So he tells us the הלכה follows רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes explaining why both rulings are needed. This step covers the second half.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's 'that week' could include the days after the fast. רבי מאיר says 'until the fast,' so ruling like him ends the restrictions at תשעה באב itself.
steps.whatToRemember: רבא's practical rule: the mourning restrictions apply only in the week of תשעה באב (like רבן שמעון בן גמליאל) and only until the fast, not after it (like רבי מאיר). Both rulings are lenient.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי אַשְׁמוֹעִינַן הֲלָכָה כְּרַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל,
phrases.english: And if he had taught us the halakha is like Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel,
I would have said: even after it,
so it teaches us the halakha is like Rabbi Meir.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי אַשְׁמוֹעִינַן הֲלָכָה כְּרַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The second side of the same צריכותא begun in step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: צריכותא: showing that each statement teaches something the other does not
steps.terutzHavaAmina: With only the ruling like רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, the restrictions would continue after the fast through the end of the week.
steps.terutzMaskana: Ruling like רבי מאיר ends the restrictions at the fast itself.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה on two cooked dishes
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's rule that on ערב תשעה באב a person may not eat two cooked dishes.
steps.simpleTranslation: On ערב תשעה באב a person should not eat two cooked dishes, and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a new topic by quoting a line from the משנה, which רב יהודה will explain next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה limits how fancy the meal before the fast can be. The next steps tell us when and at which meal this limit applies.

keyTerms.meaning: The day before the fast of the Ninth of Av
Etc.: the quote continues in the משנה

phrases.english: On the eve of the Ninth of Av

phrases.aramaic: לֹא יֹאכַל אָדָם שְׁנֵי תַבְשִׁילִין כּוּ׳.
phrases.english: a person may not eat two cooked dishes, etc.

steps.triggerLanguage: עֶרֶב תִּשְׁעָה בְּאָב לֹא יֹאכַל אָדָם שְׁנֵי תַבְשִׁילִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic: the גמרא returns to the משנה after finishing the mourning-period discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On ערב תשעה באב one may not eat two cooked dishes.

steps.title: רב יהודה: the rule applies only from midday on
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה limits the משנה: the ban on two cooked dishes applies only from six hours into the day (midday) and later. Before that it is allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: The משנה only meant from six hours of the day and later. Before six hours, it is allowed.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה narrows the משנה's rule to the afternoon.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה seemed to cover the whole day before תשעה באב. רב יהודה says it covers only from midday on, so a morning meal with two dishes is fine.

keyTerms.meaning: They only taught (this rule) in the case of...
Six hours into the day: midday

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא
phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said: They taught this only
from six hours and onward,
phrases.notes: Six hours into the day is midday, so 'onward' means the afternoon.

phrases.english: but from six hours and earlier, it is permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא מִשֵּׁשׁ שָׁעוֹת וּלְמַעְלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the time of day when the משנה's rule applies.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ban on two cooked dishes on ערב תשעה באב applies only from midday onward.

steps.title: רב יהודה: the rule applies only at the last meal before the fast
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה adds a second limit: the ban applies only to the final meal before the fast (סעודה המפסקת). At any other meal, two cooked dishes are allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב יהודה said: The משנה only meant the meal that ends eating before the fast. A meal that is not the last one is allowed.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה narrows the משנה's rule a second way: by which meal, not by time of day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even in the afternoon, the ban applies only to the סעודה המפסקת, the meal after which the fast begins. An earlier meal that is not the last one may have two cooked dishes.

keyTerms.meaning: The meal at which one stops eating before the fast (סעודה המפסקת)
A meal that is not the last one before the fast

steps.whatToRemember: According to רב יהודה, the משנה's ban on two cooked dishes is limited to the afternoon and to the last meal before the fast (סעודה המפסקת).

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא
phrases.english: And Rav Yehuda said: They taught this only
in a meal at which one stops (before the fast),

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל בִּסְעוּדָה שֶׁאֵינוֹ מַפְסִיק בָּהּ — מוּתָּר.
phrases.english: but in a meal at which one does not stop, it is permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא בִּסְעוּדָה הַמַּפְסִיק בָּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second limit from the same אמורא, this time about which meal rather than what time.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ban on two cooked dishes applies only to the סעודה המפסקת, not to other meals that day.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the special practices of the סעודה המפסקת before תשעה באב.

steps.title: Both of רב יהודה's limits are leniencies, and both are needed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says that both of רב יהודה's limits make the law easier, and that he had to say both of them.
steps.simpleTranslation: Both of these rulings are leniencies, and both of them are necessary.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא looks back at רב יהודה's two limits and says both of them make the law easier. It is setting up the next move, where it explains why each limit is needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each limit makes the ban on two cooked dishes smaller. One might think one limit is enough, so the גמרא says "וּצְרִיכָא" and promises to show why both are needed.

keyTerms.meaning: as a leniency; making the law easier
and it is necessary (to say both)

phrases.english: And both of them are leniencies,
phrases.notes: "Both" means רב יהודה's two limits from steps 6 and 7: from midday on, and only at the final meal.

phrases.english: and both are necessary.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתַרְוַיְיהוּ לְקוּלָּא, וּצְרִיכָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Comments on how רב יהודה's two limits from steps 6 and 7 relate to each other.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Both limits are leniencies, and each one is needed.

steps.title: Why the midday limit is needed
steps.stepSummary: If רב יהודה had said only 'the final meal,' we might think the ban applies even before midday. So he also said 'from six hours on.'
steps.simpleTranslation: If he had taught us only about the final meal, I would have said the ban applies even before six hours. So he teaches us: only from six hours and on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows why the midday limit is needed: the 'final meal' limit alone would leave a mistake open.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A person might eat his final meal early, before midday. With only the 'final meal' limit, we would ban two dishes at that early final meal too. The midday limit tells us the ban starts only from six hours.

keyTerms.meaning: I would have said (the mistaken first thought)

phrases.english: For if he had taught us only
about the final meal before the fast,
I would have said:
the ban applies even before six hours
so he teaches us: only from six hours and on.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאִי אַשְׁמְעִינַן בִּסְעוּדָה הַמַּפְסִיק בָּהּ, הֲוָה אָמֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the first half of the explanation promised by "וּצְרִיכָא" in step 8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: צריכותא: showing each statement teaches something the other does not
steps.terutzHavaAmina: With only the 'final meal' limit, two dishes would be banned at a final meal eaten even before midday.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ban applies only from six hours on.

steps.title: Why the final-meal limit is needed
steps.stepSummary: If רב יהודה had said only 'from six hours on,' we might think the ban applies to every meal after midday. So he also said 'only the final meal.'
steps.simpleTranslation: If he had taught us only 'from six hours and on,' I would have said the ban applies even to a meal that is not the last one. So he teaches us: only at the final meal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the other side: the midday limit alone would leave a different mistake open.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone might eat more than one meal after midday. With only the midday limit, every afternoon meal would be banned from two dishes. The 'final meal' limit tells us only the last meal before the fast is restricted.

keyTerms.meaning: a meal that is not the final meal before the fast

steps.whatToRemember: The ban on two cooked dishes on ערב תשעה באב needs both conditions: it is after midday AND it is the final meal before the fast.

phrases.english: And if he had taught us only
from six hours and on,
I would have said:
the ban applies even to a meal that is not the final one
so he teaches us: only at the final meal before the fast.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי אַשְׁמְעִינַן מִשֵּׁשׁ שָׁעוֹת וּלְמַעְלָה, הֲוָה אָמֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the second half of the explanation, the mirror image of step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: צריכותא: showing each statement teaches something the other does not
steps.terutzHavaAmina: With only the midday limit, every meal after midday would be banned from two dishes.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ban applies only to the final meal before the fast.

steps.title: There are ברייתות supporting each of רב יהודה's limits
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא announces that one ברייתא supports the first limit and another supports the second.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא was taught that matches the first version, and a ברייתא was taught that matches the second version.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up the next steps: it tells us that it will bring a ברייתא backing each of רב יהודה's two limits.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'first version' is the midday limit (step 6), and the 'second version' is the final-meal limit (step 7). The גמרא says both have support from older sources.

keyTerms.meaning: it was taught in a ברייתא

steps.confusionAlert: Here 'first version' and 'second version' are not two sides of a מחלוקת. They are רב יהודה's two separate limits, and both are accepted.

phrases.english: A ברייתא was taught like the first version.
A ברייתא was taught like the second version.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא כְּלִישָּׁנָא קַמָּא. תַּנְיָא כְּלִישָּׁנָא בָּתְרָא.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from explaining רב יהודה's limits to bringing support for them.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Each of רב יהודה's two limits is supported by a ברייתא.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports the final-meal limit
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא says that if someone plans to eat another meal on ערב תשעה באב, he may eat meat and drink wine now. If this is his last meal, he may not.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who eats a meal on ערב תשעה באב: if he plans to eat another meal, he may eat meat and drink wine. If not, he may not eat meat or drink wine.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the ברייתא that matches the second version, which limits the restriction to the final meal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא makes the restriction depend only on whether this is the last meal. That is exactly רב יהודה's second limit: the restriction applies only at the final meal.

phrases.english: It was taught like the second version:
One who eats a meal on the eve of the Ninth of Av,
if he plans to eat another meal,
he may eat meat and drink wine,
and if not,
he may not eat meat or drink wine.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא כְּלִישָּׁנָא בָּתְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Carries out the second promise of step 11.
steps.raayaObject: רב יהודה's limit that the restriction applies only to the final meal (step 7).
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that permits meat and wine if another meal will follow.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports the midday limit
steps.stepSummary: This ברייתא bans two dishes, meat, and wine on ערב תשעה באב. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says one should cut down, and רבי יהודה explains how. The ברייתא ends by saying all this applies only from six hours on.
steps.simpleTranslation: On ערב תשעה באב a person may not eat two cooked dishes, meat, or wine. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: he should change his habits. רבי יהודה explained: if he usually eats two dishes, he eats one kind. If he usually eats with ten people, he eats with five. If he usually drinks ten cups, he drinks five. This is only from six hours on, but before six hours it is all allowed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the ברייתא that matches the first version, the midday limit. The key line is the ending: 'from six hours on.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא's last line, 'בַּמֶּה דְּבָרִים אֲמוּרִים, from six hours and on,' says the restrictions start only at midday. That matches רב יהודה's first limit. The middle part shows that רבן שמעון בן גמליאל wants a person to cut back, not stop completely.

keyTerms.meaning: he should change (cut down from his usual habit)
used to; in the habit of

phrases.english: It was taught like the first version:

phrases.aramaic: עֶרֶב תִּשְׁעָה בְּאָב לֹא יֹאכַל אָדָם
phrases.english: On the eve of the Ninth of Av a person may not eat
two cooked dishes;

phrases.aramaic: לֹא יֹאכַל בָּשָׂר וְלֹא יִשְׁתֶּה יַיִן.
phrases.english: he may not eat meat and may not drink wine.

phrases.aramaic: רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר: יְשַׁנֶּה.
phrases.english: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says: he should change his habits.
Rabbi Yehuda said: How does he change?

phrases.aramaic: אִם הָיָה רָגִיל לֶאֱכוֹל שְׁנֵי תַבְשִׁילִין —
phrases.english: If he usually eats two cooked dishes,
he should eat one kind;

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם הָיָה רָגִיל לִסְעוֹד בַּעֲשָׂרָה בְּנֵי אָדָם —
phrases.english: and if he usually eats with ten people,
he eats with five;
if he usually drinks ten cups,
he drinks five cups.
When does this apply?
From six hours and on;
but before six hours, it is allowed.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא כְּלִישָּׁנָא קַמָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Carries out the first promise of step 11.
steps.raayaObject: רב יהודה's limit that the restriction applies only from six hours on (step 6).
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא's closing line: בַּמֶּה דְּבָרִים אֲמוּרִים מִשֵּׁשׁ שָׁעוֹת וּלְמַעְלָה.

steps.title: Another ברייתא: רבי מאיר bans meat and wine, and the חכמים say to cut down
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר bans two dishes, meat, and wine on ערב תשעה באב. The חכמים say a person should only reduce his meat and wine by half, and someone who does not usually have them may not have them at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another ברייתא: On ערב תשעה באב a person may not eat two cooked dishes, meat, or wine. These are the words of רבי מאיר. The חכמים say: he should change and reduce his meat and wine. How? If he usually eats a ליטרא of meat, he eats half. If he usually drinks a לוג of wine, he drinks half. If he does not usually have them at all, it is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another ברייתא on the same topic. Here the full ban is רבי מאיר's view, and the חכמים are more lenient.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the first opinion is named: it is רבי מאיר. The חכמים do not ban meat and wine. They only ask a person to cut back by half from his usual amount. But someone who does not normally have meat or wine may not start now.

keyTerms.meaning: a ליטרא, a unit of weight
a לוג, a unit of liquid measure

phrases.english: Another ברייתא teaches:

phrases.aramaic: עֶרֶב תִּשְׁעָה בְּאָב לֹא יֹאכַל אָדָם
phrases.english: On the eve of the Ninth of Av a person may not eat
two cooked dishes;

phrases.aramaic: לֹא יֹאכַל בָּשָׂר וְלֹא יִשְׁתֶּה יַיִן,
phrases.english: he may not eat meat and may not drink wine;
these are the words of Rabbi Meir.
And the Sages say: he should change his habits
and reduce his meat and wine.
How does he reduce?

phrases.aramaic: אִם הָיָה רָגִיל לֶאֱכוֹל לִיטְרָא בָּשָׂר —
phrases.english: If he usually eats a litra of meat,
he should eat half a litra;
if he usually drinks a log of wine,
he should drink half a log of wine;

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם אֵינוֹ רָגִיל כׇּל עִיקָּר — אָסוּר.
phrases.english: and if he does not usually have them at all, it is forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא אִידַּךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a parallel ברייתא that names the strict view as רבי מאיר and gives the חכמים's lenient view.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי מאיר: two dishes, meat, and wine are banned. חכמים: cut meat and wine by half, and one who does not usually have them may not have them at all.

steps.title: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל allows a usual radish or salted food after the meal
steps.stepSummary: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל adds that someone who usually eats a radish or salted food after his meal may do so on ערב תשעה באב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: if he usually eats a radish or a salted food after his meal, he is allowed to.
steps.whatsHappening: The same ברייתא ends with רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's ruling about small side foods eaten after the meal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says that a radish or salted food that a person usually eats after his meal is allowed. These small extras are not treated as a forbidden second dish.

keyTerms.meaning: he has permission; it is up to him

steps.whatToRemember: There are three levels in these ברייתות: רבי מאיר bans meat and wine, the חכמים say to cut down, and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל allows small usual extras like a radish or salted food.

phrases.english: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
If he usually eats
a radish or a salted food after his meal,
he is allowed to.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר: אִם הָיָה רָגִיל לֶאֱכוֹל צְנוֹן אוֹ מָלִיחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא from step 14 with a further leniency.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A radish or salted food that a person usually eats after his meal is allowed on ערב תשעה באב.

steps.title: Another ברייתא: the last meal versus an earlier meal
steps.stepSummary: A meal eaten because of תשעה באב forbids meat, wine and bathing. A meal not eaten because of it allows meat and wine, but bathing is still forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another ברייתא teaches: at any meal that is because of תשעה באב, a person may not eat meat, drink wine or bathe. At any meal that is not because of תשעה באב, he may eat meat and drink wine, but he may not bathe.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings one more ברייתא about eating on ערב תשעה באב. It sorts the meals into two kinds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "Because of תשעה באב" means the last meal right before the fast, the סעודה המפסקת. At that meal meat and wine are out, just like the earlier ברייתא in Step 12 said. The new detail is bathing: it stays forbidden even at the earlier meal, where meat and wine are fine.

keyTerms.meaning: Because of the Ninth of Av, meaning the final meal before the fast

steps.confusionAlert: "Not because of תשעה באב" does not mean a meal on a normal day. It is still a meal on ערב תשעה באב, just not the final meal before the fast.

phrases.english: It is taught in another ברייתא:
Any meal that is because of the Ninth of Av,
phrases.notes: He means the last meal, eaten right before the fast starts.

phrases.english: it is forbidden to eat meat
and forbidden to drink wine and forbidden to bathe.
Any meal that is not because of the Ninth of Av,
it is permitted to eat meat and to drink wine
but it is forbidden to bathe.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא אִידַּךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds one more ברייתא on the ערב תשעה באב meals and brings in the new topic of bathing.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The last meal: no meat, wine or bathing. An earlier meal: meat and wine allowed, bathing forbidden.

steps.title: Bathing follows meat
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי, quoting his father, says that whenever meat is allowed, bathing is allowed too.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ישמעאל the son of רבי יוסי says in his father's name: at any time a person may eat meat, he may also bathe.
steps.whatsHappening: A תנא disagrees with the last part of the ברייתא, the part about bathing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא forbade bathing even at the earlier meal, where meat is fine. רבי יוסי links the two rules: if meat is allowed at that meal, bathing is allowed too. Both opinions agree that at the final meal everything is forbidden.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר מִשּׁוּם אָבִיו:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yishmael, son of Rabbi Yosei, says in the name of his father:
Any time that it is permitted to eat meat,
it is permitted to bathe.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר מִשּׁוּם אָבִיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the first opinion in Step 16 about bathing at the earlier meal.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Bathing is allowed whenever eating meat is allowed.
steps.whatToRemember: At the earlier meal on ערב תשעה באב, the first opinion forbids bathing. רבי יוסי allows it, because for him bathing follows the rule for meat.

steps.title: All the practices of a mourner apply on תשעה באב
steps.stepSummary: A new ברייתא says תשעה באב has all the practices of an אבל. This includes the five bans and a ban on learning any part of תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: every practice that applies to a mourner also applies on תשעה באב. A person may not eat, drink, anoint himself with oil, wear shoes, or have marital relations. He may not read תורה, נביאים or כתובים, and he may not learn משנה, תלמוד, מדרש, הלכות or אגדות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves from the day before the fast to the fast day itself. It brings a ברייתא that lists what is forbidden on תשעה באב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא gives one big rule: treat תשעה באב like an אבל. The five physical bans are listed first. Then comes the surprise: even learning תורה is forbidden, because learning brings joy, as Step 19 will explain.

keyTerms.meaning: To learn or review תורה שבעל פה

steps.whyThisMatters: This ברייתא is the basic source for the הלכה that learning תורה is forbidden on תשעה באב.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
All the practices that apply to a mourner
apply on the Ninth of Av:
It is forbidden to eat and to drink,
and to anoint with oil, and to wear shoes,
and to have marital relations.
And it is forbidden to read in the Torah,
in the Prophets, and in the Writings,
or to study Mishnah, Talmud, and Midrash,
and halachot, and aggadot.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: כׇּל מִצְוֹת הַנּוֹהֲגוֹת בְּאָבֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the meals on ערב תשעה באב to the rules of the fast day itself.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: תשעה באב has all the practices of an אבל, including the five bans and a ban on learning תורה.

steps.title: What learning is still allowed
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא allows unfamiliar material and sad books like קינות, איוב and the harsh parts of ירמיה. Schoolchildren stop learning because תורה gladdens the heart.
steps.simpleTranslation: But a person may read a part he is not used to reading, and learn a part he is not used to learning. He may read קינות, איוב, and the bad prophecies in ירמיה. Schoolchildren stop learning, because the פסוק says: "The precepts of ה׳ are right, gladdening the heart."
steps.whatsHappening: The same ברייתא now gives exceptions to the learning ban. Then it explains the reason for the ban.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ban exists because תורה brings joy, as the פסוק says. So learning that brings no joy is allowed. Unfamiliar material is hard work rather than a pleasure, and sad books fit the mood of the day. Even children stop learning, which shows how broad the ban is.

keyTerms.meaning: Stop, take a break from learning

phrases.english: But he may read in a place
that he is not used to reading,
and he may study in a place he is not used to studying,
and he may read Lamentations and Job,
and the bad things in Jeremiah.
And schoolchildren stop learning,
because it is said:
"The precepts of ה׳ are right, gladdening the heart."

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲבָל קוֹרֵא הוּא בִּמְקוֹם שֶׁאֵינוֹ רָגִיל לִקְרוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the exceptions and the reason for the learning ban in Step 18.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Learning that brings no joy (unfamiliar material or sad books) is allowed. Joyful learning, even for children, is not.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: even unfamiliar material is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה forbids even unfamiliar material. He allows only איוב, קינות and the harsh parts of ירמיה. He agrees that children stop learning.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: a person may not even read a part he is not used to reading, or learn a part he is not used to learning. But he may read איוב, קינות, and the bad prophecies in ירמיה. Schoolchildren stop learning on that day, because the פסוק says: "The precepts of ה׳ are right, gladdening the heart."
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה disagrees with the first opinion in the ברייתא on one point: unfamiliar material.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יהודה, even learning something new and hard still brings the joy of תורה, so it is forbidden. He agrees about the sad books and about the children. The only disagreement is about unfamiliar material.

keyTerms.meaning: The bad things, meaning the prophecies of disaster

steps.whatToRemember: Everyone agrees that joyful learning is forbidden on תשעה באב and that sad books are allowed. The first opinion also allows unfamiliar material, and רבי יהודה forbids it.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
He may not even read in a place
that he is not used to reading,

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵינוֹ שׁוֹנֶה בִּמְקוֹם שֶׁאֵינוֹ רָגִיל לִשְׁנוֹת.
phrases.english: and he may not study in a place he is not used to studying.
But he may read Job and Lamentations
and the bad things in Jeremiah.

phrases.aramaic: וְתִינוֹקוֹת שֶׁל בֵּית רַבָּן בְּטֵלִים בּוֹ,
phrases.english: And schoolchildren stop learning on that day,
because it is said:
"The precepts of ה׳ are right, gladdening the heart."

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: אַף אֵינוֹ קוֹרֵא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the first opinion in Step 19 about unfamiliar material.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even unfamiliar material is forbidden. Only sad books are allowed.

steps.title: Salted meat and fresh wine are allowed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's ban on meat and wine at the last meal, then brings a ברייתא that allows salted meat and wine straight from the press.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: he may not eat meat and may not drink wine. A ברייתא taught: but he may eat salted meat and drink wine from his press.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the משנה's words about meat and wine and adds a ברייתא that gives two exceptions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ban on meat and wine is about foods that bring joy. Salted meat and unfinished wine are weaker versions that do not feel like real meat and wine, so the ברייתא allows them. This sets up the next questions about how long they must sit.

keyTerms.meaning: Salted meat that has been kept in salt for a while
Wine from his press: new wine that has not finished fermenting

phrases.aramaic: לֹא יֹאכַל בָּשָׂר וְלֹא יִשְׁתֶּה יַיִן.
phrases.english: He may not eat meat and may not drink wine.
It was taught: But he may eat
salted meat
and drink wine from his press.
phrases.notes: Freshly pressed wine that is still fermenting, not finished wine.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנָא: אֲבָל אוֹכֵל הוּא בָּשָׂר מָלִיחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the משנה's rule about the last meal after the ברייתות on learning תורה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Salted meat and wine fresh from the press are allowed at the last meal before תשעה באב.

steps.title: How long must meat be salted?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how long meat must sit in salt before it counts as 'salted meat'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Salted meat: how long?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a clarifying question about the ברייתא's term 'salted meat'. The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Meat salted for one minute is still plain meat. The גמרא wants the point at which it stops counting as meat for this rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Up to how much / how long?

phrases.english: Salted meat: up to how long?

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּשָׂר מָלִיחַ עַד כַּמָּה?
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the definition of a term from the ברייתא in step 21.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The length of salting after which meat counts as 'salted meat'.

steps.title: שמואל: measured by the time of שלמים
steps.stepSummary: רב חיננא בר כהנא, quoting שמואל, answers that the measure is the eating time of a שלמים offering.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חיננא בר כהנא said in the name of שמואל: as long as it is like שלמים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by using the time limit of the שלמים offering as the measure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שלמים may be eaten for two days and the night between them. Meat still within that span counts as fresh meat and is forbidden. Once salted meat is older than that, it no longer counts as 'meat' and is allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: Peace-offerings, which may be eaten for two days and one night

phrases.english: Rav Ḥinnana bar Kahana said
in the name of Shmuel:
As long as it is like peace-offerings.
phrases.notes: Within the שלמים eating time it is still real meat. Salted longer than that, it is allowed.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִינָּנָא בַּר כָּהֲנָא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דִּשְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 22.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Meat counts as 'salted' once it is older than the eating time of שלמים (two days and a night).

steps.title: How long is wine 'from the press'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks the same kind of question about the wine: how long does it count as 'wine from his press'?
steps.simpleTranslation: And wine from his press: how long?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a second clarifying question, this time about the wine. The answer comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question follows the same pattern as the one about meat. It asks when fresh wine turns into real wine that is forbidden at the last meal.

phrases.english: And wine from his press: up to how long?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְיַיִן מִגִּתּוֹ עַד כַּמָּה?
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Same style of question as step 22, now for the second item in the ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How long wine counts as 'wine from his press'.

steps.title: While it is still fermenting
steps.stepSummary: The answer: it counts as fresh wine as long as it is still fermenting.
steps.simpleTranslation: As long as it is fermenting.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that wine counts as 'from the press' while it is still bubbling and fermenting.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Fermenting wine is not yet real, finished wine and does not bring the same joy, so it is allowed. The גמרא has not yet said how long fermenting lasts; the next step gives that.

phrases.english: As long as it is fermenting.

steps.triggerLanguage: כׇּל זְמַן שֶׁהוּא תּוֹסֵס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 24.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Wine is allowed while it is still fermenting.

steps.title: Fermenting lasts three days
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says fermenting wine has no problem of being left uncovered, and that its fermenting lasts three days.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא taught: fermenting wine has no problem of being left uncovered. How long is its fermenting? Three days.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא from another topic, uncovered drinks, that tells us how long wine ferments.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא puts a number on 'fermenting': three days from pressing. Joined with step 25, this means wine up to three days old is allowed at the last meal before תשעה באב.

keyTerms.meaning: Leaving a drink uncovered, which was forbidden for fear a snake drank from it
The fermenting period of new wine

steps.whatToRemember: At the last meal before תשעה באב, meat salted longer than the time of שלמים and wine less than three days old are allowed, because they do not count as real meat and wine.

phrases.english: It was taught: Fermenting wine
has no problem of being left uncovered,
phrases.notes: People feared a snake might drink from an uncovered drink and leave venom. A snake keeps away from bubbling wine.

phrases.english: and how long is its fermenting?
Three days.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנָא: יַיִן תּוֹסֵס אֵין בּוֹ מִשּׁוּם גִּילּוּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the length of the fermenting period mentioned in step 25.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Wine ferments for three days, and during that time it has no problem of being left uncovered.

steps.title: How רבי יהודה ברבי אילעאי ate before תשעה באב
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה quotes רב about the custom of רבי יהודה ברבי אילעאי: on ערב תשעה באב they brought him dry bread with salt, and he would sit. The story continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: This was the custom of רבי יהודה ברבי אילעאי. On ערב תשעה באב they would bring him dry bread with salt, and he would sit...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a story about how a great תנא ate his last meal before תשעה באב. The story continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After the bare rules, the גמרא shows how far a pious person went. רבי יהודה ברבי אילעאי ate only dry bread with salt, far simpler than the law requires.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
This was the custom
of Rabbi Yehuda, son of Rabbi Ilai:
On the eve of the Ninth of Av
they would bring him dry bread with salt,
and he would sit

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב: כָּךְ הָיָה מִנְהָגוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בְּרַבִּי אִילְעַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the legal limits on the last meal to a story of one תנא's personal practice.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On ערב תשעה באב, רבי יהודה ברבי אילעאי ate only dry bread with salt.
